claims.claim: Spring Boot on Java with PostgreSQL can handle 200 small writes a second without exotic parts
claims.measured: java-spring 7,668 req/s for a single Postgres row (12,731 with virtual threads) on 1 CPU; 1,254–1,699 req/s at 20 queries per request
claims.why: The measured database throughput on one CPU is far above 200 requests a second, so the measurements support the claim.

claims.claim: A Spring Boot app with a 256 MB heap typically uses 300–400 MB resident once metaspace, threads, and code cache are counted
claims.measured: java-spring peak 220–500 MB across tests (312 MB JSON, 374 MB CPU, 491 MB I/O, 499 MB database); idle 134 MB
claims.why: The measured peaks under load range from about 220 to 500 MB, and 300–400 MB is well within a factor of 2 of that.

claims.claim: Spring Boot fits alone on a 512 MB VM, with little room to spare
claims.measured: java-spring ran in a 512 MB container with peaks up to 499–500 MB in the database tests
claims.why: It ran within 512 MB in every test, but its peaks came close to the limit, which matches 'little room to spare'.

claims.claim: Go, Node, or Python have a smaller memory footprint than Spring Boot
claims.measured: Go 7–16 MB, Node 55–77 MB, Python 41–123 MB peak vs Spring Boot 209–500 MB peak; idle Go 2 MB, Node 38–43 MB, Python 40–115 MB vs Spring 131–134 MB
claims.why: All three use clearly less memory than Spring Boot in every test, so the direction of the claim is correct.

claims.claim: Heavy JPA/Hibernate uses more memory and CPU than plain JDBC, JdbcTemplate, or jOOQ
claims.why: The benchmark does not compare data-access libraries within Spring Boot.

claims.claim: Quarkus or Spring Boot native images (GraalVM) give much lower memory and faster startup
claims.why: Neither Quarkus nor native-image builds were measured; only JVM Spring Boot (5,939–6,224 ms start-up, 131–134 MB idle) is in the data.
